chapter: War years, Goodman and Woody Herman
title: William Morris big band with Johnny Thompson arrangements
summary: Morris wants a Norvo big band; he forms a band of woodwinds and brass with arranger Johnny Thompson, plays with Mildred and records 'I'll Be Around'.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well, actually how that came about was just before that, after I broke up with MCA, I was deciding what to do, I had a little group at the Hickory House -- with Aaron and, you know, some more people -- Remo Palmieri, (unintelligible) and Ned Williams came to me and said, that William Morris, Jr., wanted me to get a band department. He wanted Duke Ellington and he always liked the band that I had in the '30's, so
he wanted me to get a big band. So I did. I got -- I formed a band. Five woodwinds and six brass. And three rhythm.
Um.

And with that 10-piece band we had, we played down in Dallas and I'd met a kid -- a fella there that was going to Julliard when I was playing at the Commodore. Mildred and I were. And, he was back home and he came around and he made a couple of arrangements. Talented kid. So I said if I decide to to get the big band, I was trying to make up my mind whether it was a good move or not --
Yeah?
I said I'd like for you to be the arrangement, because at that time Eddie Sauter had gone with Goodman and doing some very wonderful things. Like Benny Rides Again, and that band.
Yeah.

And I didn't think that he'd be available. So, Johnny Thompson was his name and he was getting married and he was going to California on his honeymoon and suddenly he read in one of the trade magazines that I was forming a band, so they changed their mind and came to New York. And walked in this first day of rehearsal, I nearly fell over. And, he started to write for that band. So, Eddie did a few things; Alec Wilder did a couple of things --
Yeah, I was going go -- to ask you.
The book was very, very good. The book was a very fine book.
Well just --
And we played Blue Gardens and we did Mildred joined us and we did theater dates with Jimmy Durante. For about three or four months.
Because I remember that -- some of the things that Mildred was singing, out at -- Alec Wilder had done the arrangements. So was that the time?
Well I think he did a couple of woodwind things with Teddy and Roy Eldridge, we're on, remember he had a -- I don't know what date that was. I think he did "All The Things You Are," I'm not sure.
Oh, yeah.
Eddie Sauter did most of those, but I don't know what --
Well it was --
Well I know he did a couple for Mildred at that time.
Right.
But he did some for this band, special material things.
Yeah.
And at that time he did "I'll Be Around," which we did and we did do a record of that, and that's the

band that's on that record. MS. VANCE: Oh, I see. MR. NORVO: And, it was an amazing record, when you think that the record ban was starting that day and we did -- Mildred had did five shows with a cold at the Paramount and so hoarse she couldn't talk. And we went over to Lederkranz Studio and recorded four sides, one of them was I'll Be Around and how she ever sang, I'll never know. She sang over that cold and made that record.
After the Paramount too --
Huh?
After the Paramount -- after the shows --
Yeah, five shows at -- how did -- she did it, I'll never know.
Gosh.

But then we went on the road and it was quite a nice band, it was a great show band, well written and five saxophones and the woodwinds, they all doubled like flute -- we had English horn and oboe -- great rhythms. And then --
How about that?
-- six -- three trombones and three trumpets.
How about that? Did you --
